mainTopic: Garment-scrap wicks and רבי עקיבא's retraction, indirectly adding oil to a lamp on שבת, dragging benches according to רבי שמעון, and the start of the משנה on extinguishing a lamp.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the ברייתא about a three-by-three-finger cloth scrap. If it was put in a box, everyone agrees it can still become טמא. רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about a scrap hung on a peg or left behind a door. רבי עקיבא first split the two cases between them, and later switched fully to רבי יהושע's view, which רבא proves from the wording 'פתילת הבגד' in our משנה. A new משנה then forbids feeding a lamp extra oil on שבת from an eggshell, an earthenware tube, or a separate bowl, while רבי יהודה permits all three. The גמרא explains why each case had to be listed, and adds that a firm attachment like a potter's makes it one vessel, which is permitted. רבי יהודה tries to prove his view from the silence of רבי טרפון and the elders in בית נתזה, and the חכמים reject the proof because those people were especially careful. Two stories about dragging a bench lead to a debate between עולא and רבי ירמיה רבה about how far רבי שמעון's leniency goes, and רבה's proof from the clothing merchants refutes רבי ירמיה רבה. Finally, a new משנה begins about putting out a lamp on שבת: out of fear or for a sick person one is פטור, to save the lamp, oil, or wick one is חייב, and רבי יוסי makes him חייב only for the wick.

steps.title: Defining exactly where the dispute applies
steps.stepSummary: If the cloth was stored in a box, all agree it can become טמא. The argument is only about hanging it on a peg or placing it behind a door.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he put it in a box, everyone agrees it can become טמא. They only argued when he hung it on a peg or put it behind a door.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. It tells us which case is agreed upon and which cases are actually in dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting the cloth in a box shows the owner still values it, so it keeps the status of a garment and can become טמא. Hanging it on a peg or leaving it behind a door is a middle case: he did not throw it away, but he also did not store it carefully. That middle zone is where the argument lives.

keyTerms.meaning: A box or chest for storing things carefully
A peg or rack on the wall for hanging things

phrases.english: If he placed it in a box —
everyone agrees it is susceptible to impurity.
phrases.notes: Storing it in a box shows he plans to use it.

phrases.english: They only disagreed where he hung it on a peg
or where he placed it behind the door.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of the ברייתא about the three-by-three cloth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A box means everyone agrees it is טמא. A peg or behind the door is the disputed case.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's reasoning
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds that since he did not throw it in the garbage, he still has it in mind. He called it 'not prepared' only in comparison to a box.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר holds: since he did not throw it in the garbage, he still has it in mind. So why did he call it 'not prepared'? Because compared to something kept in a box, it is not prepared.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי אליעזר says the cloth on the peg can still become טמא. It also explains his word 'שלא מן המוכן' (not prepared).
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר measures against the garbage heap. Not throwing it away shows the owner still cares about it, so it stays a garment. His phrase 'not prepared' is only relative: it is less ready for use than a cloth in a box, but it was not thrown away.

keyTerms.meaning: His mind is on it (he still intends to use it)
Not from the prepared (not set aside for use)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'not prepared' as meaning רבי אליעזר thinks the cloth is useless. He means only that it is less prepared than one in a box. He still holds it can become טמא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer holds:
since he did not throw it into the garbage heap,
his mind is on it.
And why does he call it 'not from the prepared'?
Because compared to a box, it is not prepared.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first side of the disputed case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cloth on a peg or behind the door keeps its garment status because it was not thrown away.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's reasoning
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע holds that since he did not put it in a box, he has nullified it. He called it 'prepared' only in comparison to the garbage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע holds: since he did not put it in a box, he has nullified it. So why did he call it 'prepared'? Because compared to something in the garbage, it is prepared.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יהושע says the cloth on the peg is no longer a garment. It also explains his word 'מוכן' (prepared).
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע measures against the box. Not storing it carefully shows the owner gave up on it as a garment. His word 'prepared' is also only relative: it is more prepared than garbage, but it is still nullified.

keyTerms.meaning: He has definitely nullified it (cancelled its garment status)

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides use relative language. רבי אליעזר compares to the garbage (not thrown away, so it is still important). רבי יהושע compares to the box (not stored, so it is nullified).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua holds:
since he did not place it in a box,
he has certainly nullified it;
and why does he call it 'prepared'?
Because compared to the garbage heap, it is prepared.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of רבי אליעזר's reasoning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cloth on a peg or behind the door loses its garment status because it was not stored in a box.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא splits the two cases
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא follows רבי אליעזר for a cloth hung on a peg, and רבי יהושע for a cloth behind the door.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא: when he hung it on a peg, he holds like רבי אליעזר. When he put it behind the door, he holds like רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי עקיבא's middle position. He agrees with each side in a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hanging something on a peg looks like keeping it, so it stays a garment and can become טמא. Tossing it behind a door looks like giving up on it, so it is nullified.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva:
where he hung it on a peg, he holds like Rabbi Eliezer;
where he placed it behind the door,
he holds like Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, בִּתְלָאוֹ בְּמַגּוֹד סָבַר כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the third opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Peg means not nullified. Behind the door means nullified.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא changed his mind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that רבי עקיבא later retracted and fully adopted רבי יהושע's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא retracted and came over to רבי יהושע's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds new information: רבי עקיבא's split view was not his final position. This sets up a request for proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רבי עקיבא holds that even a cloth hung on a peg is nullified. This would explain why, in our משנה, he calls a garment-wick טהור.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva retracted
to the view of Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Updates רבי עקיבא's position from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא's final view matches רבי יהושע's.

steps.title: How do we know he retracted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the claim that רבי עקיבא retracted.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for evidence. This short question sets up רבא's proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A claim that a תנא changed his mind needs textual support. The answer will come from the exact wording of our משנה.

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for proof of step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that רבי עקיבא adopted רבי יהושע's view.

steps.title: רבא's proof from the phrase 'wick of the garment'
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that the משנה says 'פתילת הבגד', which implies the wick is still a garment. Even so, רבי עקיבא rules it טהור, so he must hold like רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: since the משנה says 'פתילת הבגד'. Why say it that way? It could have said 'a wick made of a garment.' Why 'פתילת הבגד'? Because it is still a garment.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא proves the retraction from a careful reading of the wording in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'wick OF THE GARMENT' signals that the folded cloth still counts as a garment. It is not just a wick that used to be cloth. Yet רבי עקיבא says it is טהור and may be lit. That means he considers even something still close to a garment to be nullified, just like רבי יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it teach (it should have said)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא draws legal positions from tiny differences in a משנה's wording.

phrases.english: Rava said:
From the fact that it teaches 'the wick of the garment.'
Why specifically does it teach 'the wick of the garment'?
Let it teach 'a wick made of a garment.'
What does 'the wick of the garment' mean?
That it is still a garment.
phrases.notes: Yet רבי עקיבא calls it טהור, which matches רבי יהושע's view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: רבי עקיבא's retraction to רבי יהושע's view.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording 'פתילת הבגד' in the משנה, together with רבי עקיבא's ruling that it is טהור.

steps.title: New משנה: an oil-filled eggshell over the lamp
steps.stepSummary: One may not attach an oil-filled pierced eggshell, or an earthenware version of it, over a lamp to drip in oil. רבי יהודה permits. If the potter attached it from the start, it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may not pierce an eggshell, fill it with oil, and place it over the mouth of the lamp so it drips oil in. This applies even if it is made of earthenware. רבי יהודה permits it. But if the potter attached it from the start, it is permitted, because it is one vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It discusses adding a separate oil reservoir to a burning lamp on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים fear that a person might take oil out of the separate reservoir. Taking oil from a burning lamp makes it go out sooner, which is like extinguishing. When the reservoir is built into the lamp as one vessel, people treat it as part of the lamp and will not take from it, so it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: An eggshell (a hollow tube of egg)

phrases.english: MISHNAH: A person may not pierce
the shell of an egg
and fill it with oil
and place it over the mouth of the lamp
so that it will drip,
and even if it is of earthenware.
And Rabbi Yehuda permits it.
But if the potter attached it from the outset —
it is permitted, because it is one vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ לֹא יִקּוֹב אָדָם שְׁפוֹפֶרֶת שֶׁל בֵּיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A separate oil reservoir is forbidden according to the חכמים and permitted according to רבי יהודה. One built into the lamp is permitted.

steps.title: משנה continued: a bowl of oil beside the lamp
steps.stepSummary: One may not place a bowl of oil next to the lamp with the wick's end inside it to draw oil. רבי יהודה permits.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may not fill a bowl with oil, place it beside the lamp, and put the end of the wick inside it so the wick draws oil. רבי יהודה permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third case of feeding the lamp extra oil, this time from a separate bowl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the reservoir is not attached to the lamp at all. It sits beside the lamp and is connected only by the wick. The same argument applies: the חכמים forbid it and רבי יהודה permits it.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְמַלֵּא אָדָם קְעָרָה שֶׁל שֶׁמֶן
phrases.english: A person may not fill a bowl with oil
and place it beside the lamp
and put the end of the wick into it
so that it will draw oil.
And Rabbi Yehuda permits it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא יְמַלֵּא אָדָם קְעָרָה שֶׁל שֶׁמֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third case to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bowl is forbidden according to the חכמים and permitted according to רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Why both the eggshell and the earthenware are needed
steps.stepSummary: With the eggshell alone, we might think the חכמים would permit earthenware, which is disgusting. With earthenware alone, we might think רבי יהודה would forbid the eggshell.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary to teach both. If the משנה taught only the eggshell, I would say the חכמים forbid it because it is not disgusting and a person might take oil from it. But earthenware is disgusting, so I would say they agree with רבי יהודה. If it taught only earthenware, I would say רבי יהודה permits only that one, but for the eggshell he agrees with the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a צריכא to explain why the משנה lists several cases. This step covers the first pair: eggshell and earthenware.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the prohibition is the fear that someone will take oil from the reservoir. A clean eggshell invites taking oil. A dirty clay tube does not. So each case could have been treated differently, and each must be written: earthenware shows the חכמים forbid even there, and the eggshell shows רבי יהודה permits even there.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is necessary (to teach each case)
To take (oil) from it for his own use

steps.confusionAlert: The 'I would say' lines are only a possible mistaken assumption (הוה אמינא). They are not the actual law.

phrases.english: GEMARA: And it is necessary.
For if it had taught us only the eggshell —
in this case the Rabbis say it is forbidden,
since it is not disgusting
he may come to take oil from it.
But earthenware, which is disgusting —
I would say they agree with Rabbi Yehuda.
And if it had taught us only earthenware —
in this case Rabbi Yehuda says it is permitted,
but in that case (the eggshell) —
I would say he agrees with the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes why the משנה needed multiple cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both cases are needed because the 'disgusting' factor could change each side's view.

steps.title: Why the bowl case is also needed
steps.stepSummary: With only the two attached cases, we might think רבי יהודה forbids the separate bowl. With only the bowl, we might think the חכמים permit the attached cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the משנה taught only those two, I would say רבי יהודה permits them because they are not separate from the lamp, but for a bowl, which is separate, he agrees with the חכמים. If it taught only the bowl, I would say the חכמים forbid only that, but for the two others they agree with רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the צריכא with the second pair: the two attached reservoirs compared with the separate bowl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new factor appears: whether the reservoir is physically separate from the lamp. The bowl case shows רבי יהודה permits even when it is separate. The two attached cases show the חכמים forbid even when it is not separate.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only those two,
in these Rabbi Yehuda says it is permitted
because it is not separated,
but a bowl, which is separated —
I would say he agrees with the Rabbis.
And if it had taught us only that one (the bowl),
in that one the Rabbis say it is forbidden,
but in these two —
I would say they agree with Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the צריכא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bowl case and the attached cases are each needed because of the 'separated' factor.

steps.title: Conclusion: every case is necessary
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that all the cases in the משנה are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore it is necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the צריכא. Each case in the משנה teaches something the others could not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two factors could have changed the law: whether the reservoir is disgusting and whether it is separate from the lamp. Listing all the cases shows that the חכמים forbid every version and רבי יהודה permits every version.
steps.whatToRemember: The argument is the same in all three cases. Neither 'disgusting' nor 'separate' changes the view of the חכמים or of רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: It is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the צריכא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three cases in the משנה are needed. Each answers a different possible mistaken assumption.

steps.title: A homeowner's firm attachment also counts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling about a potter's attachment and adds a ברייתא: attaching the shell with plaster or potter's clay is also permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if the potter attached it from the start, it is permitted. A ברייתא teaches: if he attached it with plaster or with potter's clay, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the potter clause of the משנה, the line right after the eggshell case. Then it brings a ברייתא that seems to widen that ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the shell is firmly stuck to the lamp, it becomes one vessel with the lamp. Taking oil from it would then count as putting out the lamp, so no one will take oil from it. The ברייתא says a person can create that same firm attachment himself, using plaster or clay.

phrases.english: And if the potter attached it from the start
it is permitted, etc.
It was taught: if he attached it
with plaster or with potter's clay, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא אִם חִבְּרָהּ בְּסִיד וּבְחַרְסִית מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the last clause of the משנה after the discussion of why every case was needed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A firm attachment with plaster or clay is permitted, just like a potter's attachment.

steps.title: But the משנה said a potter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא, because the משנה specifically mentions a potter.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned 'potter' in the משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the ברייתא can permit a homeowner's attachment when the משנה names only a potter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording 'potter' suggests that only a professional's attachment works. If so, a homeowner using plaster should not be enough, and the ברייתא would contradict the משנה.

phrases.english: But we learned 'potter'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא from the wording of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא that permits a homeowner's attachment
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה names a potter, which implies that a layman's attachment does not count.

steps.title: Potter means an attachment like a potter's
steps.stepSummary: 'Potter' in the משנה describes the kind of attachment, not the person who makes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'potter' mean? An attachment similar to a potter's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the word 'potter' in the משנה differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה cares about how strong the attachment is, not about who made it. Any firm attachment that works like a potter's, such as plaster or clay, is permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: What matters is a firm, potter-like attachment, not whether a professional made it.

phrases.english: What is 'potter'?
Like a potter('s attachment).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a real potter's attachment is permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any attachment as firm as a potter's is permitted.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's story in Lod
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה tells how they used a pierced eggshell over a lamp in front of רבי טרפון and the elders, and no one objected.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: Once we spent שבת in the upper room of בית נתזה in לוד. They brought us an eggshell, and we filled it with oil, pierced it, and placed it over the lamp. רבי טרפון and the elders were there, and they said nothing to us.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא records רבי יהודה bringing a real-life proof for his lenient opinion about the eggshell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה argues that the great sages' silence shows they agreed it was permitted. Silence from a great sage while watching an action is treated as approval.

keyTerms.meaning: Upper room of the house of Nitza

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda said:
One time we spent Shabbat
in the upper room of the house of Nitza in Lod,
and they brought us an eggshell
and we filled it with oil and pierced it
and placed it over the mouth of the lamp.
And Rabbi Tarfon and elders were there,
and they did not say anything to us.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה פַּעַם אַחַת שָׁבַתְנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the argument between רבי יהודה and the חכמים about the eggshell
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's ruling permitting the eggshell
steps.raayaSupportSource: The silence of רבי טרפון and the elders when they saw the eggshell used

steps.title: The people of בית נתזה were careful
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject the proof, because the people there were especially careful.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Is that a proof? בית נתזה is different, because they are careful.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי יהודה's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry behind the prohibition is that someone will take oil from the shell. Those sages were careful people who would never do that, so the elders had no reason to object there. Ordinary people are not that careful, so the prohibition still stands for everyone else.

phrases.english: They said to him: From there a proof?!
The house of Nitza is different,
for they are careful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. The case is limited to careful people.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The elders kept silent only because the people there were careful. Their silence does not mean the practice is allowed for everyone.

steps.title: Silence can cause damage
steps.stepSummary: אבין dragged a bench on a marble floor. רבי יצחק בן אלעזר spoke up, so his silence would not be mistaken for approval the way the elders' silence was with רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבין ציפוראה dragged a bench in a marble upper room in front of רבי יצחק בן אלעזר. He said to him: If I stay silent with you, the way the group stayed silent with רבי יהודה, damage will come of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that uses the eggshell episode as a warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The elders' silence led רבי יהודה to wrongly conclude that the eggshell was permitted. So רבי יצחק בן אלעזר objected out loud, even though the floor was marble. He did not want anyone to learn a wrong leniency from his silence.

keyTerms.meaning: Upper room with a marble floor

steps.confusionAlert: Dragging on marble cannot make a furrow. The objection was about the false lesson people would learn, not about the act itself on marble.

phrases.english: Avin of Tzippori dragged a bench
in an upper room of marble
before Rabbi Yitzchak ben Elazar.
He said to him: If I am silent to you
as the colleagues were silent to Rabbi Yehuda,
damage will come out of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָבִין צִיפּוֹרָאָה גְּרַר סַפְסַלָּא בְּעִילִּיתָא דְשֵׁישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the eggshell story as a lesson about protesting
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sage should protest so that his silence is not taken as permission.

steps.title: Why a marble floor is also forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Dragging on a marble floor is forbidden as a גזירה, because of ordinary earth floors.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree: a marble upper room because of an ordinary upper room.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why dragging the bench on marble was a problem at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On an earth floor, dragging a bench digs a furrow, which is like plowing. The חכמים also forbade it on marble, so people would not confuse the two kinds of floors.

phrases.english: A decree: a marble upper room
because of an ordinary upper room.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵירָה עִלִּיתָא דְשֵׁישָׁא אַטּוּ עִלִּיתָא דְעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the halachic basis of the objection in step 18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dragging on marble is forbidden as a גזירה because of earth floors.

steps.title: Even רבי שמעון only permits large benches
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה challenges a man who dragged a bench. רבי שמעון permitted dragging only large benches, not small ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: The head of the synagogue of בצרה dragged a bench in front of רבי ירמיה רבה. He said to him: Whose opinion are you following, רבי שמעון's? Say that רבי שמעון permitted large benches, which cannot be moved any other way. Did he say so about small ones?!
steps.whatsHappening: Another bench story. A sage challenges the person who dragged it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון permits an act when the forbidden result, a furrow, is not intended (דבר שאין מתכוין). רבי ירמיה claims רבי שמעון said this only about large benches, which must be dragged. A small bench can be carried, so even רבי שמעון would not permit dragging it.

keyTerms.meaning: Which is impossible (to move another way)

phrases.english: The head of the synagogue of Batzra
dragged a bench
before Rabbi Yirmeya the Great.
He said to him: According to whom? Rabbi Shimon?
Say that Rabbi Shimon said it
about large ones, which are impossible (to move otherwise);
about small ones, did he say it?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story on the same topic of dragging benches
steps.kashyaTarget: The man's dragging of a small bench
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון's leniency applies only to large benches that cannot be moved any other way.

steps.title: This disagrees with עולא
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה's view disagrees with עולא. עולא holds that the dispute is about small benches, and large benches are permitted according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagrees with עולא. For עולא said: The dispute is about small ones, but about large ones everyone agrees it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי ירמיה's approach conflicts with עולא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי ירמיה, the dispute is about large benches, and small ones are forbidden by everyone. According to עולא, large benches are permitted by everyone, and רבי שמעון disagrees with רבי יהודה only about small ones. So according to עולא, רבי שמעון does permit dragging small benches.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי ירמיה: רבי שמעון permits only large benches. עולא: large benches are permitted by all, and the dispute is about small ones.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Ulla.
For Ulla said:
The dispute is about small ones,
but about large ones, all agree it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Notes that another אמורא holds differently from רבי ירמיה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to עולא, large benches may be dragged according to everyone, and the dispute is only about small ones.

steps.title: A ברייתא that seems hard for both עולא and רבי ירמיה רבה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes a ברייתא where רבי שמעון allows dragging a bed, a chair, and a bench. Because it mentions both large and small items, it seems to contradict both עולא and רבי ירמיה רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: רבי שמעון says a person may drag a bed, a chair, and a bench, as long as he does not intend to make a groove in the ground. The ברייתא includes large items and small items, so it is hard for both of them!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא to challenge both sides of the argument from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A chair is small. So according to רבי ירמיה רבה, who says רבי שמעון forbids small benches, the ברייתא is a problem. A bed is large. According to עולא, everyone already allows large items, so why would רבי שמעון need to say it? One list causes trouble for both views.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection (from a written source)
A groove or furrow in the ground
As long as he does not intend
It is difficult for both of them

phrases.english: Rav Yosef raised an objection:
Rabbi Shimon says
a person may drag a bed, a chair, and a bench,
as long as he does not intend to make a furrow.
phrases.notes: This is רבי שמעון's well-known principle of דבר שאין מתכוין.

phrases.english: It teaches large items (a bed) and it teaches small items (a chair),
so it is difficult for both of them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges both positions that were just set side by side in Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: Both רבי ירמיה רבה's view (small benches forbidden for רבי שמעון) and עולא's view (large benches allowed by everyone).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's list has a small item that רבי שמעון allows, which goes against רבי ירמיה רבה. It also has a large item that would not need mentioning, which goes against עולא.

steps.title: Each side reads the ברייתא his own way
steps.stepSummary: עולא says the 'bed' in the ברייתא is a small bed, like a chair. רבי ירמיה רבה says the 'chair' is a heavy chair, like a bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא answers according to his view, and רבי ירמיה רבה answers according to his view. עולא: the bed is like the chair, meaning a small bed. רבי ירמיה רבה: the chair is like the bed, meaning a large, heavy chair.
steps.whatsHappening: Each אמורא answers רב יוסף's objection by reading the list in the ברייתא so that it fits his own opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For עולא, every item in the list is small, so the ברייתא is about small items, which is exactly where רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה disagree. For רבי ירמיה רבה, every item in the list is large and too heavy to lift, which is the only kind רבי שמעון allows. Both views survive this objection. Step 24 brings a new challenge that decides between them.

keyTerms.meaning: Answers according to his own reasoning

phrases.english: Ulla answers according to his reasoning
and Rabbi Yirmeya the Great answers according to his reasoning:
Ulla answers according to his reasoning —
the bed is like the chair.
phrases.notes: A small, light bed that could be picked up like a chair.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yirmeya the Great answers according to his reasoning —
the chair is like the bed.
phrases.notes: A big, heavy chair that can only be moved by dragging.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּלָּא מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ וְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה רַבָּה מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's objection for both sides.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the ברייתא's list so that all items fall into one size category.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא mixes large and small items, so it fits neither view.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each side reads the list as one uniform category (all small for עולא, all large for רבי ירמיה רבה).

steps.title: The clothing merchants prove רבי שמעון allows even small items
steps.stepSummary: רבה quotes a משנה: clothing merchants may wear כלאים garments while selling them, as long as they do not intend to benefit. Even though they could carry them on a stick like the צנועין, it is allowed. So רבי שמעון allows even when there is another way, like small benches.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה objected: Clothing sellers may sell in their normal way (wearing the garments of כלאים on their shoulders), as long as they do not intend to use them for protection from the sun or from the rain. The צנועין would hang them on a stick behind them. Now here, it is possible to act like the צנועין, which is just like small benches that could be lifted instead of dragged. Yet when he does not intend, רבי שמעון allows it from the start!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה brings a משנה to challenge רבי ירמיה רבה, who said רבי שמעון forbids dragging small benches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The merchant has an easy alternative: he could carry the clothes on a stick and avoid any question. Still, the משנה (following רבי שמעון) allows him to wear them לכתחילה, as long as he does not intend to benefit. That is exactly like a small bench that could be lifted. So רבי שמעון should allow dragging small benches too.

keyTerms.meaning: Hang on a stick over the shoulder

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is about כלאים, not שבת. רבה uses it only to show how far רבי שמעון's rule of 'no intention means permitted' goes, even when there is an easy way to avoid the problem.

phrases.english: Rabba raised an objection:
Clothing sellers may sell in their normal way,
phrases.notes: Even placing garments of wool and linen on their shoulders.

phrases.english: as long as he does not intend
in the sun, for protection from the sun,
or in the rain, for protection from the rain,
and the modest ones hang them on a stick behind them.
Now here, where it is possible to act like the modest ones —
which is like small benches,
phrases.notes: Small benches can be lifted instead of dragged, just as clothes can be carried on a stick.

phrases.english: and when he does not intend —
Rabbi Shimon permits it from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both sides survived רב יוסף's objection, רבה brings a new source aimed only at רבי ירמיה רבה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה רבה's claim that רבי שמעון forbids dragging small benches.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי שמעון allows wearing כלאים without intention even when an easy alternative exists, he should also allow dragging small benches, which also have an easy alternative (lifting).

steps.title: רבי ירמיה רבה's view is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares a full refutation of רבי ירמיה רבה, and confirms it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רבי ירמיה רבה. It is indeed a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא announces that רבה's objection completely knocks down רבי ירמיה רבה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תיובתא means there is no answer, so the view is rejected. The result is that עולא's reading stands: רבי שמעון allows dragging even small benches when there is no intention to make a groove.

keyTerms.meaning: A complete refutation, with no answer

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, as long as one does not intend to make a groove, he may drag even small benches. Large benches are allowed by everyone (עולא). רבי ירמיה רבה's narrower view was refuted.

phrases.english: This is a refutation of Rabbi Yirmeya the Great.
It is indeed a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes that רבה's objection has no answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי ירמיה רבה is refuted. רבי שמעון permits dragging even small benches without intention.

steps.title: New משנה: putting out a lamp on שבת
steps.stepSummary: Someone who puts out a lamp out of fear, or so a sick person can sleep, is פטור. Someone who puts it out to save the lamp, the oil, or the wick is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who puts out the lamp because he is afraid of non-Jews or of robbers, or because of a bad mood, or so that a sick person can sleep, is exempt. If he does it to save the lamp, to save the oil, or to save the wick, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, teaching when putting out a flame on שבת makes a person פטור and when it makes him חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference depends on why he puts out the flame. In the first group he only wants the darkness, not anything about the lamp itself, and he is פטור. In the second group he wants to save the lamp, oil, or wick, and he is חייב. The גמרא will explain the reasons later.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (start of a new משנה)
A bad spirit, a depressed mood
Like one who wants to spare or save

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who extinguishes the lamp
because he is afraid
of non-Jews or of robbers,
because of a bad spirit,
or for the sick person, so that he will sleep —
is exempt.

phrases.aramaic: כְּחָס עַל הַנֵּר, כְּחָס עַל הַשֶּׁמֶן,
phrases.english: If he does it to spare the lamp, to spare the oil,
or to spare the wick —
he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמְכַבֶּה אֶת הַנֵּר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מִתְיָרֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic after the bench discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Extinguishing out of fear or for a sick person is פטור. Extinguishing to save the lamp, oil, or wick is חייב.

steps.title: רבי יוסי exempts in all cases except the wick
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the person is פטור in all these cases, except when he puts out the flame to save the wick, because then he is making charcoal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי exempts him in all the cases, except for the wick, because he turns it into charcoal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees with the first opinion in the משנה, which made the person חייב in all three 'saving' cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, putting out a flame by itself is not a full Torah-level מלאכה in these cases. Only saving the wick counts, because putting it out leaves a charred tip, which is like making charcoal, and that makes it easier to light later. So only that case makes him חייב.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא makes one חייב when he puts out a flame to save the lamp, oil, or wick. רבי יוסי makes him חייב only for the wick, because he is making charcoal.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei exempts in all of them,
except for the wick —
because he makes it into charcoal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a disagreeing opinion within the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: פטור in all cases except saving the wick, which is חייב because it creates charcoal.
